hotspots.title: Congress Avenue Bridge Bats
hotspots.subtitle: World's largest urban bat colony · sunset emergence Mar–Nov

info.description: Roughly 1.5 million Mexican free-tailed bats stream out from under the Ann W. Richards Congress Avenue Bridge at dusk each evening from mid-March to early November. Watch from the bridge sidewalk, the Statesman Bat Observation Center, or a kayak on Lady Bird Lake.

hotspots.title: Mount Bonnell
hotspots.subtitle: Highest natural point in Austin · panoramic Hill Country overlook

info.description: 775 feet up via 102 stone steps. Sweeping views of Lake Austin, the Pennybacker Bridge, and the Hill Country. Open daily 5 AM–10 PM. Free.

hotspots.title: South Congress (SoCo) District
hotspots.subtitle: Vintage shops, food trucks, murals · the iconic Austin strip

info.description: Walkable stretch of South Congress Ave between Riverside and Live Oak. Shops, taco trailers, music venues, and a postcard-skyline view looking north toward the Capitol.

hotspots.title: Pennybacker Bridge Overlook
hotspots.subtitle: Cliffside view of the Loop 360 arch bridge

info.description: Short scramble from the small dirt parking lot on the south side of Loop 360 leads to the cliff overlook of Percy V. Pennybacker Jr. Bridge — Austin's signature arch over the Colorado River. Best at golden hour.
Painted on the side of Roadhouse Relics in 1998 by Todd Sanders and Rory Skagen. The classic Austin tourist photo.

hotspots.title: "I love you so much" Mural
hotspots.subtitle: Jo's Coffee · 1300 S Congress · most-photographed wall in town

info.description: Scrawled in red on the side of Jo's Coffee in 2010 by musician Amy Cook for her partner. A line forms most mornings for the photo.

hotspots.title: "Hi, How Are You?" Mural
hotspots.subtitle: Daniel Johnston's Jeremiah the Innocent · 21st & Guadalupe

info.description: Daniel Johnston painted the wide-eyed frog on the side of what's now Thai How Are You in 1993. The mural sits at the corner of 21st & Guadalupe across from the UT campus.

hotspots.title: Treaty Oak
hotspots.subtitle: 500-year-old live oak · Treaty Oak Park · 507 Baylor St

info.description: Estimated 500 years old and once the centerpiece of a 14-tree grove called the Council Oaks, sacred to the Comanche and Tonkawa. Famously poisoned in 1989 and nursed back to health.

hotspots.title: Cathedral of Junk
hotspots.subtitle: Vince Hannemann's 60-ton folk-art sculpture · by appointment

info.description: A three-story castle of welded scrap in a South Austin backyard at 4422 Lareina Dr. Visits by appointment only — call ahead. Donation appreciated.

hotspots.title: 6th Street Entertainment District
hotspots.subtitle: Austin's historic main strip · the live-music-bar mile

info.description: Old Pecan Street, between Congress and I-35. Music clubs, dive bars, and rooftops. Closes to cars on weekend nights.

hotspots.title: Rainey Street Historic District
hotspots.subtitle: Converted-bungalow bar street between downtown and Lady Bird Lake

info.description: Two blocks of early-1900s bungalows turned into bars and food trucks, tucked between downtown and the lake. Short walk to the Boardwalk Trail.

hotspots.title: Stevie Ray Vaughan Statue
hotspots.subtitle: Auditorium Shores · bronze with downtown-skyline backdrop

info.description: Ralph Helmick's 1993 bronze of Austin's most famous guitarist on the north lawn of Auditorium Shores, framing the downtown skyline across Lady Bird Lake.
